meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Panama (National Jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Panama-United States Trade Promotion Agreement (effective 31 October 2012)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 (AML/CFT framework), as amended by Law 70 of 2017; Executive Decree 133 of 2017 (beneficial ownership identification and reporting); Executive Decree 168 of 2017 (transparency of legal persons); Private Interest Foundations are governed by Law 25 of 12 June 1995 and its amendments; UBO records are maintained by the Panamanian Public Registry and are accessible to competent authorities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the founding beneficiary's passport biographical page
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport issuing authority or notary public in the document's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement issued within the last three months)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank, utility provider, or notary public in the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of incumbency or registry extract if the founder is a legal person
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registry or company registrar in the founder's jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization for non-Hague Contracting States

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Sworn declaration of beneficial ownership, source of funds, and intended economic activity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the jurisdiction where the founder executes the declaration

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original bank reference letter evidencing financial standing and account conduct
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution where the founder has maintained an account for a meaningful period

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all founders, council members, protectors, and named beneficiaries against the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list, OFAC SDN list, EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and Panama's domestic Ministry of Economy and Finance risk and PEP registers. Conduct enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds verification, and senior-management approval for any positive PEP or sanctions-related match. Adverse media and reputational risk screening is performed through licensed AML data providers before acceptance of the foundation mandate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Sistema en Línea de Reserva de Nombres (online name reservation module)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Foundation names may be expressed in Spanish or any language using Latin script. The name must convey or include the word 'Fundación' or 'Foundation' to indicate the entity's nature. A non-Latin script name must be transliterated into Latin script for registry purposes and must be sufficiently distinguishable from existing registered names.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or confusingly similar to existing registered companies, foundations, or protected trademarks
Words implying sovereign, governmental, or international status without authorization (e.g., 'Estado', 'Central', 'Nacional', 'Gobierno')
Regulated financial and fiduciary terms requiring prior ministerial approval (e.g., 'Banco', 'Seguros', 'Fideicomiso', 'Valores', 'Bolsa', 'Financiero')
Names contrary to Panamanian law, public morals, or public order
Names incorporating public or international institutions such as 'Panamá', 'ONU', 'Banco Mundial', or 'Cruz Roja' without proper consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Within five working days of the refusal notice, the registered agent may file an administrative reconsideration petition with the General Directorate of the Registro Público de Panamá. The petition must restate the proposed name, attach evidence of the name-search result, and, where applicable, include written consent or disclaimer from the holder of a conflicting name. If the second review is unfavourable, the applicant may either immediately reserve a different available name or pursue judicial review before the Administrative Contentious Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court within two months. The 30-day reservation is not extendable, but a new reservation can be filed after expiration.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is permissible for administrative correspondence only. The statutory registered office of a Panamanian Private Interest Foundation must be the physical address of the licensed resident agent in Panama. A post-office-box-only address or an unregistered virtual address is not accepted as a statutory registered office.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low standard risk: approximately 3-5% annual probability of registered-agent file inspection by the competent supervisor. Unannounced physical inspections are possible in a risk-based AML/CFT examination, but the expected likelihood for a non-financial PropTech holding foundation is under 10% in any given year.

Notarial execution and certification of the Private Interest Foundation charter

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Beneficial ownership registry / competent AML authority

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed resident agent and registered office services - first year

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark under Law 25 of 1995

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille, and consular legalization of founder due diligence documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Fixed compliance due diligence fee based on market rates

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley No. 25 de 12 de junio de 1995 (Private Interest Foundations Law), as amended, Articles 4–7 (Foundation Charter contents, endowment, registration and legal personality) and Article 13 (Foundation Council), together with implementing Executive Decree No. 92 of 12 September 1995.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) — Private Interest Foundations Section (Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Foundation Charter (Acta de Constitución) executed as a public deed before a licensed Panamanian Notary Public and presented for inscription
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum foundation endowment of USD 10,000 (B/.10,000) or equivalent in lawful assets; no escrow or bank deposit is required, as a notarial declaration of endowment in the Foundation Charter suffices for registration; the annual state franchise tax thereafter is USD 300.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDATION COUNCIL OF [NAME] FOUNDATION, a Private Interest Foundation of the Republic of Panama constituted by public deed under Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995, unanimously adopted in writing on [date]. RESOLVED: 1. The initial endowment of USD 10,000 declared by the Founder is ratified and accepted. 2. The registered office is fixed at [address], Ciudad de Panamá, Republic of Panama. 3. [Name A] is appointed initial Member and [Name B] alternate Member of the Foundation Council, each with full powers. 4. [Name C] is appointed Protector under Law No. 25. 5. The Resident Agent services of [Agent] are confirmed. This Resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Notarial Execution of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Notary Public of Panama City (Notaría Pública del Circuito), acting under the authority of the Supreme Court of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panamanian attorney to draft the Foundation Charter (Acta de Constitución) including the registered name ending with 'Fundación', foundation object (management of the PropTech/SaaS platform assets, intellectual property and shares), Founder details, initial endowment, members of the Foundation Council, Protector, beneficiaries, registered office, Resident Agent letter and liquidation provisions. The Founder executes the public deed in person or by power of attorney before the Notary. The Notary records the deed in the protocol and issues notarial testimony for registration.
required_dossiers: KYC/due diligence documentation for Founder, Foundation Council members and Protector
Power of attorney (if Founder is represented)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If counsel or the Notary identifies formal defects before execution, amend the draft and re-notarize without additional registry penalty.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Public Registry Tariff and Panama Stamp Tax
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) — Fiscal and Collections Window (Tesorería del Registro Público)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Request the tariff assessment based on the endowment bracket. The statutory filing tariff for a foundation endowment of up to USD 10,000 is approximately USD 150, to which the notarial stamp tax on the public deed of approximately USD 100 is added. Pay at the designated collection window or authorized bank and obtain the official receipt as proof of payment.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry recalculates the tariff differently, the difference is paid before filing or a refund is credited; amended receipts are reissued within the same business day.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing and Inscription with the Registro Público de Panamá
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Registry of Panama (Registro Público de Panamá) — Private Interest Foundations Section
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial testimony, the tariff payment receipt and the Resident Agent's cover letter to the Foundations Section. The Registry examiner verifies compliance with Law No. 25 of 1995, including name uniqueness, endowment, domicile, council and Resident Agent. Upon approval, the Foundation is inscribed and the Registration Certificate (Certificado de Inscripción) is issued. Legal personality attaches exclusively upon inscription.
required_dossiers: Original notarial testimony of the Foundation Charter
Cover letter or report by Resident Agent
Certified copy of the public deed for the Registry file
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: A Registry 'reparo' (technical objection) is cured by filing a written clarification or a corrective notarial instrument within the statutory term; the re-presented application receives priority review without new filing fees.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration and Issuance of RUC Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: General Directorate of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos — DGI) via the Sede Electrónica online taxpayer portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the inscribed Foundation in the Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) using the certificate of inscription; file the Aviso de Operación declaring the commencement of ISIC 6201 software development and SaaS activities; obtain the RUC certificate and enable the taxpayer account for monthly ITBMS returns and annual income tax filings.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Inscripción from the Public Registry
Identity documents of Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the DGI queries the application, submit additional supporting evidence via the Sede Electrónica within five business days; the provisional RUC remains valid until the final authorization is resolved.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Business License and Fire and Civil Defense Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality of Panama (Alcaldía de Panamá) — Municipal Treasury (Tesorería Municipal), single business window
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the municipal Operating License application (Aviso de Operación Municipal) for the registered office of the SaaS platform; declare the estimated gross annual revenue to determine the municipal operating tax. Simultaneously request the Fire Safety Certificate for the premises from the Panamanian Fire Department (Dirección General de Bomberos de Panamá) following an on-site inspection of the physical office area.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Inscripción from the Public Registry
Lease agreement or property title for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality inspects and queries building occupancy standards, present the building completion certificate and land-use certificate (Certificado de Uso de Suelo); a contested tax assessment may be appealed before the Municipal Treasury within 15 business days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce and Industries of Panama (MICI) — General Directorate of Industrial Property; no industrial or manufacturing permit is applicable to ISIC 6201 cloud-based property management software services
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No industrial operating permit is required; the authorizations applicable to the registered office are the municipal Operating License (Aviso de Operación Municipal), the RUC tax registration, and the Fire Safety Certificate.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment of Panama (Ministerio de Ambiente — MiAMBIENTE)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — no EIA registration or full Environmental Impact Assessment report is required because the activity is a purely digital SaaS and property-technology service with no physical industrial installation, no point-source discharges and no land-use change; General Environmental Law No. 41 of 1998 does not subject office-based information services to an EIA.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero industrial discharge applicable. If the registered office connects to municipal sewerage, comply with effluent quality standards in Executive Decree No. 12 of 2017; any refrigerant or backup power equipment must satisfy MiAMBIENTE atmospheric emission norms; electronic waste must be transferred to a MiAMBIENTE-registered e-waste handler.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate issued by the Dirección General de Bomberos de Panamá after an on-site inspection of the registered office; building occupancy and land-use certificate (Certificado de Uso de Suelo) issued by the Municipality of Panama; occupational health and safety compliance under the Ministry of Labor and Labor Development (MITRADEL) for all employees, including a workplace risk assessment and emergency evacuation plan.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF); taxpayer portal: Sede Electrónica de la DGI (https://sede.dgi.gob.pa)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) deriving Panamanian-source taxable income must first obtain a Registro Único de Contribuyentes (RUC) from the DGI. The DGI does not issue a separate TIN; the RUC serves as the unified tax identification number for income tax, VAT (ITBMS), and payroll taxes. The foreign entity or PIF must: (1) complete and file the standardized RUC application form through the Sede Electrónica portal or at an authorized DGI office; (2) submit the Public Registry foundation deed and certificate of incorporation; (3) provide notarized proof of the entity's registered address in Panama; (4) appoint a resident legal representative or fiscal agent where the PIF has no domestic management; (5) submit identification documents of the foundation council members and protector (if any); and (6) obtain a digital taxpayer certification (token/firma digital) for e-filing. After RUC activation, the taxpayer must also register for electronic invoicing and ITBMS.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Panama's territorial tax system taxes only Panamanian-source income. There is no U.S.-style check-the-box election; entity classification follows the legal form of the PIF and its activity in Panama. A PIF is generally treated as a taxable legal entity for Panamanian-source income, but distributions to beneficiaries are not taxed at the foundation level if the foundation holds assets passively. Available elections include: (a) election to use the Código Fiscal cost basis and depreciation rules for asset holding; (b) election under Article 698 et seq. to be taxed on a remittance basis for foreign-source dividends and interest; and (c) limited transitional elections for relief under ratified tax treaties (no comprehensive double tax treaties except for specific multinational agreements). Hybrid mismatch elections are not statutorily available; Panama's participation in the BEPS Inclusive Framework does not incorporate EU ATAD-style hybrid rules into domestic law.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_tax_regime_for_foreign_entities: Panama territorial taxation with entity-level tax on Panamanian-source income, no capital gains tax on foreign asset sales, and no tax on worldwide income.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Corporales Muebles y Servicios (ITBMS) — VAT system
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general exemption threshold. Any person or entity supplying taxable goods or services in Panama—including cross-border digital services to Panamanian customers—must register for ITBMS if they carry on habitual or occasional taxable activities. There is a simplified small-taxpayer regime for entities with annual gross receipts up to PAB 36,000 that substitutes for full ITBMS compliance. Foreign SaaS providers with no Panamanian establishment are required to register through the simplified e-Tax non-resident registration procedure if they make B2C supplies to Panamanian consumers; there is no numeric threshold beyond the small-taxpayer rule.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Panama operates a mandatory fiscal electronic invoicing regime (Factura Electrónica) implemented progressively by DGI resolutions (especially Res. No. 055-2017 and subsequent enforcement resolutions). Taxpayers must: (1) obtain authorization as an electronic invoicing issuer; (2) use DGI-approved invoicing software or an authorized technology provider; (3) transmit invoices in near-real-time to DGI's electronic platform (Sede Electrónica) for validation; (4) include the DGI-assigned eight-digit fiscal folio, authorization string, and QR code; and (5) receive the DGI electronic acceptance/rejection response before issuing the final document to the customer. The regime also mandates a digital stamping and clearance mechanism for invoices above statutorily defined amounts. The DGI has imposed monetary fines and suspension of the RUC for non-compliant issuers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.applicable_cross_border_digital_services: Cross-border digital services (SaaS, cloud, remote software) supplied by foreign entities to Panama customers are subject to ITBMS at 7%. The DGI requires foreign digital service providers to register and levy ITBMS through the simplified 'proveedor extranjero de servicios digitales' mechanism. The foreign supplier may recover input ITBMS only where related to Panamanian taxable supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods and certain internationally rendered services qualify for 0% ITBMS. For physical goods: the goods must be definitively exported from Panama and must be substantiated by a customs export declaration. For services: the service must be rendered to a non-resident recipient, effectively consumed outside Panama, and not directly connected to Panamanian real property. For a PropTech SaaS provider, hosted/cloud software services to foreign clients qualify for 0% where (i) the recipient is outside Panama, (ii) the service is delivered electronically from Panama, and (iii) no Panamanian real estate is directly managed or evaluated on behalf of the foreign client except on a purely incidental basis. Services connected to the management of real estate physically located in Panama remain subject to 7% ITBMS even if the client is abroad. The zero rate may only be applied after the exporter obtains the required documentation and files the export declaration with the DGI.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Declaración de Exportación) duly accepted by the Autoridad Nacional de Aduanas (ANA) for goods
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill (where physical shipment is involved)
Final commercial invoice with explicit 'Exportación / 0% ITBMS' annotation
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificación de Compensación de Divisas) issued by a Panamanian licensed bank showing receipt of foreign currency within the repatriation deadline
Preferential Certificate of Origin (if applicable under trade agreements)
Service agreement or contract with the non-resident client evidencing offshore service delivery and place-of-consumption clauses
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI and the Comisión de la Bolsa / AML authorities scrutinize export zero-rating claims through bank-foreign currency reconciliation. If the exporter fails to repatriate export proceeds within 180 days without valid justification or fails to provide the mandated documentation on audit, the zero rate is invalidated and the 7% ITBMS becomes due retroactively. Penalties include: (a) 100% of the omitted tax as a fine for fraudulent zero-rating; (b) a monthly 1.5% late interest surcharge on underpaid ITBMS; (c) suspension of the RUC and electronic invoicing authorization; and (d) potential criminal sanctions under the Código Fiscal for tax fraud, including imprisonment for amounts exceeding USD 100,000. The DGI may also impose fines of PAB 500–10,000 for documentary procedural irregularities, and the statutory limitation period for audit is six years, extendable to ten in fraud cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP); Panama has no separate central bank and operates on a full US dollar standard. Monetary and exchange rate policy are effectively determined by the US Federal Reserve, with SBP overseeing regulatory compliance for all banking and trust activities.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama maintains full and unrestricted convertibility of the US dollar. Capital account transactions, profit repatriation, dividends, and current account transfers are freely permitted without prior exchange control approval. No surrender requirements, no repatriation delays, and no restrictions on foreign ownership of bank accounts. The legal tender is exclusively the US dollar; no local fiat currency exists to convert.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Panama imposes no statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio on export receipts, SaaS subscription proceeds, or any inbound cross-border payments. All USD receipts may be held indefinitely, reinvested, or remitted abroad without exchange control filings.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Operating Account / Foreign Currency Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bac International Bank, Inc. S.A. (BAC Credomatic)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Operating Account / Merchant Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility: Medium (restricted). Panama does not yet have a comprehensive Electronic Money Institution (EMI) licensing regime. Offshore digital EMIs (e.g., Mercury, Payoneer, Wise Business) generally rely on correspondent arrangements through US or European banks and can open accounts for a Panama PIF on a discretionary basis. Key constraints include enhanced due diligence on the foundation's structure, the need for a Panamanian legal opinion, and the risk of sudden debanking without local regulatory recourse. A dedicated Panamanian bank account remains the legally safest and most stable solution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For Tier 1 Panamanian banks, at least one authorized signatory and the beneficial owner (or a formally designated officer with power of attorney) must attend a physical or video-notarized KYC interview. Several banks now permit remote onboarding via secure video call supplemented by apostilled constitutional documents and a notarized certification of signature. However, for escrow and capital injection accounts, physical presence at the bank's head office in Panama City is typically mandated unless a long-term private client relationship already exists.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Private Interest Foundation with undisclosed beneficiaries and broad object clauses.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the Foundation Charter (Pacto Fundacional), Rules Regulations (Reglamento), current certificate of registration from the Public Registry of Panama, legal opinion from a Panamanian counsel identifying settlor, foundation council members, beneficiary and protector, plus a detailed organizational chart showing ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and source of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PropTech income inconsistent with the foundation's stated commercial profile.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Audited or management-prepared financial statements for the last two years, commercial contracts with property management clients, software licensing agreements, SaaS platform user statistics, and a detailed business plan describing the digital real estate screening service and payment flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Inbound capital injection from jurisdictions classified as high-risk or lacking adequate KYC standards.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements from the originating institution, source-of-wealth declaration, tax residence certificates of all investors, and evidence of the economic substance in Panama (physical office, local board minutes, and operational records) to demonstrate legitimate cross-border capital movement.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursements to third-party vendors in dissimilar industries or to high-risk geographies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Original invoices, executed vendor agreements, webhosting and cloud infrastructure contracts, and a funds flow matrix showing the commercial rationale. For payments to related parties, transfer pricing documentation and a consolidated organizational chart are required.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital must be routed via SWIFT MT103 wire transfers in USD to the PIF's Panamanian bank account. The wire message must include a clear purpose code per the receiving bank's classification, typically 'Capital Contribution' (code 201) or 'Investment in Private Equity' (code 203). For foundations, the legal name on the wire must exactly match the registered corporate name on the foundation certificate. Verification requires the transferor to send proof of identity and entitlement (e.g., a board resolution for corporate investors) to the receiving bank prior to the first credit. Payment networks ACH and domestic Panama clearing (ACH-P) may be used only for local operating expenses from the same account.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for subscription fees, licensing, cloud infrastructure, and vendor payments are executed through USD SWIFT MT103 wires, with the Panama clearing house (ACH-P) available only for local utility or payroll transactions. Letters of credit (Commercial LCs) are permissible for physical asset acquisitions but are uncommon for SaaS. For cross-border ACH disbursements, the PIF will need a US correspondent routing number or a fintech aggregate provider; direct US ACH is not natively available without a US-based account. All outbound wires require supporting documentation as per AML requirements and must align with the foundation's permitted business scope.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: USD/EUR non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) with offshore counterparties (not locally regulated)
USD/GBP currency swaps executed through an international bank branch licensed in Panama
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for managing foreign-currency loan risk
Spot USD purchase against foreign currencies received (no restriction under Panamanian law)
Forward contracts through US correspondent banks for non-USD revenue exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Franchise Tax (Tarifa Anual de Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas; validated against the Registro Público de Panamá
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before January 31 of each calendar year; annual fee applies irrespective of the PIF’s formation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge if paid in February; 20% surcharge if paid in March or later; after 24 months of unpaid fees, the Registro Público may refuse to act on foundation certificates; continuous non-payment for 3 years triggers administrative strike-off or cancellation proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Registry Confirmation (Confirmación Anual del Registro de Beneficiario Final)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) – Registro Único de Beneficiario Final (RUBF)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 following the close of the prior calendar year; interim updates must be filed within 15 days after any change in ownership or foundation certificate transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines per late filing ranging from US$100 to US$5,000; continued non-compliance may suspend the PIF’s good-standing certificate and block filings at the Registro Público.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) – only if Panama-source taxable income exists
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI), Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Due on or before March 31 of each year for the preceding calendar year; incorporated PIFs with no Panama-source income are not required to file an active income-tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharge of 10% of the tax due plus monthly interest accrual; refusal or repeated failure to file may trigger fines up to US$25,000 and restriction of the PIF’s commercial registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is mandatorily required for a standard dormant Private Interest Foundation. An independent certified audit becomes compulsory if the PIF engages in Panama-source commercial activity and either (a) annual gross revenues exceed US$250,000, or (b) total assets exceed US$1,000,000, or (c) the foundation charter or a competent court expressly requires audited accounts for a particular fiscal year.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS (as endorsed by the Panamanian Association of Certified Public Accountants) or IFRS for SMEs for entities without public accountability. Accounting books must be kept in a manner consistent with Panama’s territorial tax regime.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Resident Agent must maintain the Beneficial Owner Register and transmit an annual declaration to the DGI’s Registro Único de Beneficiario Final by March 31. Any transfer of rights under the foundation certificates, changes in the beneficiary list, or substitution of the Foundation Council must be recorded in the statutory registers and reported to the Resident Agent as an interim confirmation within 15 days of the event, accompanied by a resolution of the Foundation Council.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Foundation Certificate Holders (equivalente al Registro de Miembros)
Register of Foundation Council Members (equivalente al Registro de Directores)
Minute Book of the Foundation Council (Libro de Actas)
Beneficial Owner Register maintained by the Resident Agent

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$600 – US$1,200 per year for licensed resident agent and registered office services in Panama City
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$2,500 – US$8,000 per audit engagement depending on transaction volume, asset complexity, and use of local certified public accountants

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Territorial taxation applies: the Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) pays 25% corporate income tax exclusively on Panama-source income. Foreign-source SaaS subscription, rental-screening, and IP licensing revenue is outside the Panamanian tax net. The PIF's initial endowment and accumulated foreign-source wealth are exempt from Panama income tax, and beneficiary distributions are not taxed as income of the foundation. No general tax holiday exists for the ISIC 6201 PropTech segment; however, capital expenditures on software development are capitalizable and amortizable, payroll and cloud infrastructure costs are deductible, and the territorial source rule yields a 0% effective rate on foreign-derived subscription revenue.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 400 (Declaración Jurada de Renta – Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DGI electronic portal (Servicios en Línea, dgi.gob.pa) of the Dirección General de Ingresos, Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year taxpayers, the standard PIF fiscal year, the return is due on 31 March of the following year. Monthly advance payments (anticipos) of ISR are remitted by the 15th of each month.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) of the PIF, legal name, NIT, address, and registered agent details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the foundation's Panama tax ID; designate the Foundation Council member with Panamanian residence who will act as responsible party before the DGI.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: All Panama-source gross income, including SaaS cloud subscription fees, rental-screening data processing, and software license revenue from Panamanian clients.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Panama-source revenue; foreign-source SaaS payments are excluded, but the filer must preserve contracts, client use locations, and technical routing evidence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Ingresos Exentos y No Gravables
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-source revenue, export service income, and other non-Panama-source receipts segregated from global gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach a schedule listing foreign clients and place-of-use certifications; the amount allocated offshore must be supported by contemporaneous substance documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Direct costs, cloud infrastructure expense, salaries, depreciation, amortization, and interest directly allocable to Panama-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany technical service fees and IP royalties require arm's-length substantiation; non-resident founder fees are challengeable without a transfer pricing Local File.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after deductions (Box 2 less Box 4).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Distributions to PIF beneficiaries are not deductible; the PIF must add back any such distribution to the taxable base.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax computed at 25% on the net taxable income reported in Box 5.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If no Panama-source income is generated, file with B/. 0 (zero) tax, but disclose global business activity and request an annual clearance certificate to substantiate the zero position.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for monthly advance payments made during the fiscal year and for withholding taxes previously imposed on the PIF's Panama-source receipts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividends distributed to non-resident beneficiaries cannot be credited against the PIF's income tax liability; withholding at the beneficiary level is a separate charge.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 8 – Saldo a Pagar o a Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final net tax due to the DGI after Box 7 credit, or tax credit to be refunded or carried forward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A refund claim by a foreign-owned PIF will trigger FATCA/CRS exchange and enhanced beneficial-ownership review; maintain full Portuguese? (removed) -- maintain full legal, bank, and beneficiary documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory transfer pricing annex for taxpayers with cross-border related-party transactions above the statutory threshold; contains intercompany contracts, functional analyses, and financial ratios.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: PropTech SaaS intercompany subscriptions, management fees, and IP royalty payments to or from the PIF must be fully documented in the annex.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing attracts an administrative fine of B/. 50 to B/. 10,000, plus a 10% surcharge on the unpaid tax. Delayed payment accrues monthly interest at 1% (12% per annum). Failure to file for more than 12 months permits the DGI to issue a default assessment with an additional 20% penalty. Failure to remit anticipos triggers the same monthly interest plus a 10% late-payment charge.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficiary must obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (Certificado de Residencia Fiscal) from the home tax authority, legalize or apostille the certificate, and deliver it to the Panamanian withholding agent before distribution. The withholding agent files the certificate together with the corresponding withholding return and annexes before the DGI. Application of reduced rates under Panama's DTAs (Singapore, Mexico, the United Arab Emirates, South Korea, and others) occurs at source after DGI validation; the competent authority may require additional beneficial-ownership declarations and underlying contract evidence in respect of the PIF structure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 12.5% final withholding applies to Panama-source payments for software licenses, trademarks, patents, and technical assistance where the IP is used in Panama; treaty rates may reduce withholding to 5%–10%. Interest: Panama does not impose withholding tax on interest paid to a non-resident lender without a permanent establishment in Panama (territoriality); the domestic rate is 0%, and treaty rates also apply at 0% where the DTA provides an exemption.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: B/. 1,000,000 (USD 1,000,000) in cross-border related-party transactions per fiscal year, or classification as a Gran Contribuyente with gross annual revenue above B/. 10,000,000, triggers the Local File. Reporting groups with consolidated revenue of EUR 750 million file a Master File and Country-by-Country Report under BEPS Action 13. The DGI may require contemporaneous documentation for smaller transactions where it identifies margin erosion or insufficient substance.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Panama does not maintain standalone Economic Substance Regulations comparable to the UAE. Nevertheless, the territorial tax system, anti-abuse principles, and judicial doctrine of simulation require a PIF to demonstrate substantive Panama-based presence: local management, payroll or contracted service providers, bank accounts, accounting records, and risk-bearing capacity. A PIF that merely holds legal title to the PropTech SaaS operation while all decisions and operations occur abroad is exposed to DGI re-characterization as a shell, at which point the foreign-source exclusion and the dividend withholding exemption may be disregarded and the underlying economic owners assessed at 25% on Panama-source receipts.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission or falsification of Panama-source SaaS revenue in Form 400, creation of fictitious deductions, or fraudulent application of the territorial exclusion to revenue earned from Panamanian customers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal conviction is punishable by imprisonment of 2 to 5 years and a fine of up to B/. 500,000; the civil re-assessment computes the 25% ISR plus a 10% late-payment surcharge and 1% monthly interest; an additional 100% penalty on the evaded tax is imposed for filing a false return.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Foundation Council members and officers are jointly and severally liable for withheld taxes not remitted. Directors who sign or direct a fraudulent declaration face criminal prosecution, personal civil restitution, DGI travel bans (restricción de salida), and embargo of personal assets.
